0.tr: Episode 1: Paella (or how I embarrassed myself with César's mother)

1.tr: Hi, you're listening to "Spanish for False Beginners".
v: Part of the progressive estás escuchando: an action happening right now.
g: Describes what is happening at this very moment: estás escuchando = you are listening (now).

4.tr: On that same website you'll also be able to memorise the vocabulary flashcards, so you can learn the new words you're going to hear in the episode.
k: same (here: esa misma página = that very same page)
v: ir a + infinitive: future plans → vas a poder = you will be able to.
After ir a. Poder itself is then followed by another infinitive (memorizar).
vas a escuchar = you are going to hear.
o: relative pronoun = las nuevas palabras, the object of escuchar
g: vas a poder = you'll be able to. Very common spoken way to talk about the future instead of the future tense (podrás).
que vas a escuchar describes las nuevas palabras; que is the object of escuchar.

5.tr: My name is César, I'm a Spanish teacher from Spain, and in this podcast we're going to help you learn Spanish if you're a "false beginner" — in Spanish, un falso principiante.
k: teacher (masc.); profesor de español = Spanish teacher
false beginner: someone who has studied before but feels like a beginner
v: ser for identity: mi nombre es César.
ser for profession and origin (soy profesor, de España).
ir a + infinitive: what we plan to do.
The object pronoun te is attached to the end of the infinitive.
ayudar a + infinitive = to help (someone) to do.
o: you, the listener (attached to ayudar: ayudarte)
g: With ser + profession Spanish uses no article: soy profesor (not *soy un profesor).
With ir a + infinitive the pronoun can go on the end (vamos a ayudarte) or before ir (te vamos a ayudar). Same meaning.
ayudar takes the preposition a before the next verb.
si + present indicative for a real, possible condition: if you are…

6.tr: Maybe you speak or have studied another European language, or you even studied Spanish, but a few years ago.
k: language (masculine: el idioma, despite ending in -a)
v: quizás + subjunctive expresses more doubt; quizás + indicative (as in sentence 7: entiendes) sounds more certain.
Auxiliary of the present perfect subjunctive: hayas estudiado.
Preterite: a completed period in the past (hace unos años).
o: otro idioma europeo (what you speak / have studied)
g: After quizás / tal vez you can use the subjunctive (more doubt) or the indicative (more likely).
haya + participle in a subjunctive context: hayas estudiado = you may have studied.
hace unos años = a few years ago.

7.tr: Or maybe you simply already understand very well, but the result is the same: podcasts for beginners seem too easy to you, and you want a challenge.
v: Stem change e → ie (entender → entiendes). Indicative after quizás = the speaker thinks it's likely.
Agrees with los pódcasts (the subject), not with te.
o: you, the listener: the podcasts seem easy TO YOU
g: te parecen fáciles = they seem easy to you. The thing (los pódcasts) is the subject; the person is an indirect object pronoun.
ya = already. Very frequent; also 'now' or for emphasis.

v: estar for location: aquí está = here it is.
g: Fixed way to present something: here it is!

9.tr: I already have another podcast, for intermediate-level students, in case you're interested.
v: Singular because the subject is the other podcast (it interests you).
o: you: it is of interest TO YOU
g: te interesa = you're interested (lit. it interests you).
por si = in case; normally followed by the indicative.

v: Pronominal verb llamarse = to be called.
g: se llama = it's called / its name is. Me llamo, te llamas, se llama…

11.tr: In this new adventure I'm not alone, I'm accompanied by the Englishman.
v: estar + adjective for a current state: estoy solo, estoy acompañado.
g: estar + participle describes a state: estoy acompañado = I have company. It agrees with the subject (acompañado, masc. sg.).
solo (adjective) = alone; it agrees: estoy solo / estoy sola.
Use bien (adverb), not bueno: estoy bien = I'm fine.

x: How are things? / How about…? Very common informal greeting.

v: estar for how you feel right now.

17.tr: Really happy to start, to begin this podcast with you, honestly.
v: Synonym of empezar; he corrects/repeats himself.
g: Adjective + de + infinitive: happy to do something.
x: honestly / to tell the truth (used at the start or end of a sentence)

18.tr: I think we have to tell the person who is listening to us who you are, and why you can help them learn and improve their Spanish.
v: creo que + indicative: stating an opinion.
Inside the relative clause que nos escucha.
In Spain le is often used for a person as direct object (leísmo).
o: (decirle) to la persona que nos escucha — doubled: le … a la persona
us (the two hosts): the person who listens to US
(ayudarle) the listener. Strictly ayudar takes a direct object (lo/la); using le for a person is common in Spain (leísmo).
g: Spanish repeats the indirect object: decirle (le) a la persona. le is normally kept even when the person is named.
Question words keep their accent inside a sentence: quién eres, por qué puedes.
su is ambiguous; here it means the listener's.

19.tr: Well, I'm a teacher too, like you, César.
g: como tú = like you. After como use tú, not ti.

20.tr: I'm a language teacher too, although not of Spanish.
g: aunque + indicative states a fact (although); with the subjunctive it means 'even if'.

21.tr: Besides, I also like learning languages.
v: Singular: the subject is the infinitive phrase aprender idiomas.
Infinitive as the subject of gustar.
o: me: it is pleasing TO ME
g: me gusta + infinitive = I like doing. With an infinitive gustar is always singular.

22.tr: I'm English, as you can tell from my accent, and I started learning Spanish a few years ago.
k: se nota = it shows, you can tell
v: Spelling change z → c before e (empecé). Preterite for a completed event at a past moment.
o: the Spanish he started to learn
g: se nota = it shows / one can notice.
hace algunos años = some years ago.
Nationalities and languages are not capitalised in Spanish: soy inglés, hablo español.

23.tr: I really like the language and I hope my experience and the mistakes I've made can help other students like me.
k: to commit/make (cometer un error = to make a mistake)
v: esperar que = to hope that → triggers the subjunctive.
Present perfect: mistakes made up to now.
Subjunctive after esperar que (wish/hope). Plural: mi experiencia y los errores.
o: relative pronoun = los errores (the mistakes I have made)
g: Verbs of hope/wish + que + subjunctive when the subject changes: espero que puedan…
Actions in a period that reaches the present: the mistakes I have made (so far).

24.tr: Well, Englishman, you speak Spanish very well, you're not a "false beginner",
g: Spanish usually drops tú; saying it adds emphasis/contrast.

26.tr: But tell me, why don't you tell us your real name?
v: Affirmative command: the pronoun is attached and an accent is added (cuenta → cuéntame). contar = to tell.
Present used in a question as a suggestion: ¿por qué no…? = why don't you…?
g: Pronouns attach to affirmative commands: cuéntame, dímelo. A written accent keeps the original stress.
A friendly suggestion: why don't you…?

27.tr: I'm a bit shy, to be honest.

28.tr: I think I prefer you to call me 'the Englishman' for now.
v: Stem change e → ie; preferir que triggers the subjunctive.
Subjunctive after preferir que with a different subject (I prefer that YOU call me).
g: Preference about someone else's action → subjunctive.
x: for the time being, for now

29.tr: I want to keep my anonymity!
v: Same subject, so infinitive (not que + subjunctive).

31.tr: Well, Englishman, today we've come to talk about paella and about what happened when you met my mother.
v: Present perfect with hoy (a period that includes now).
venir a + infinitive = to come to do.
conocer in the preterite = to meet someone for the first time.
o: a mi madre — personal a before a person as direct object
g: Time expressions that include the present (hoy, esta semana) take the present perfect in Spain.
conocí a tu madre = I met your mother (for the first time).
A specific person as direct object is preceded by a.

32.tr: The Englishman and I are a couple — that is, we're in a romantic relationship — and we live together in London, in England.
k: boyfriends / a couple (novio = boyfriend; novios = a couple)
g: juntos agrees with the subject (two men → masc. plural).
x: that is (to say), in other words

33.tr: Five years ago we travelled to Spain and the Englishman met my family.
v: Same form as the present; hace 5 años shows it's past.
conocer in the preterite = to meet for the first time.
o: a mi familia (personal a: a group of people)
g: For -ar and -ir verbs the nosotros form is the same in present and preterite; context decides.

34.tr: For such a special occasion my mother cooked paella.
v: Completed action at that past moment.
g: una ocasión tan especial = such a special occasion.

35.tr: I'm from Valencia, the region of Spain where the most typical dish is paella, Valencian paella.
g: el plato más típico = the most typical dish.
la región donde = the region where.

36.tr: Do you remember the recipe for this paella?

o: la receta (feminine singular, from the previous question)
g: la replaces a feminine singular noun: la receta → la recuerdo.

38.tr: The truth is I was very surprised when I saw the paella your mother had cooked.
v: la verdad es que = the truth is that.
Imperfect for a state/feeling in the past.
Preterite for the single moment he saw it.
había cocinado = had cooked (before he saw it).
o: relative = la paella, object of había cocinado
g: estaba sorprendido = background state; vi = a single completed action.
An action completed before another past action: she had cooked it before he saw it.

39.tr: In my mind, Spanish paella was rice with seafood.
v: Imperfect for a belief/description in the past.

40.tr: Seafood is the animals we eat from the sea.
v: Agrees with los animales (plural) rather than el marisco.

41.tr: But the paella I saw on the table was something very different.
g: algo diferente = something different (adjective after algo, masculine form).

42.tr: Lots of people are surprised when they find out the original paella recipe, the traditional recipe.
v: cuando + indicative for something that happens habitually.
o: la receta original de la paella
g: sorprender = to surprise (someone); sorprenderse = to be surprised.
For general/habitual situations cuando takes the indicative; for the future it takes the subjunctive.

43.tr: Tell us, what was in the paella? What ingredients did it have?
k: (of food) to contain, have in it
v: Imperfect to describe what the paella was like.
g: ¿Qué lleva? = What's in it? Very common when talking about dishes.

44.tr: What struck me most were the snails, or as the French say, the 'escargots'.
k: to strike, make a strong impression
g: lo que más me impactó = the thing that struck me most.
lo que … fueron los caracoles: the verb agrees with the plural noun.

45.tr: I never thought I was going to find snails in a paella.
v: A completed thought at that moment.
ir a in the imperfect = 'was going to' (future seen from the past).
g: The past of ir a: what was going to happen from a past point of view.

46.tr: I have to say I've never tried them, I've never eaten them with paella.
v: Present perfect with nunca: experience up to now.
Same structure: nunca los he comido.
g: nunca + present perfect = never (in my life so far).
With compound tenses the pronoun goes before haber: los he probado.

47.tr: The idea seemed a bit disgusting to me; it's a very slimy animal.
v: Imperfect for an opinion/feeling over time.
o: me (César): it seemed disgusting TO ME
g: la idea me parecía = the idea seemed (to me)…

49.tr: Now I don't eat any animal because I'm vegan — that is, I don't eat anything of animal origin.
k: no, not any (before a masc. sg. noun: ningún)
g: Spanish uses double negatives: no como ningún animal / no como nada.

50.tr: Why do you vegans always have to say that you're vegan?
v: vosotros form, used in Spain for 'you all'.
g: A noun group the speaker addresses ('you vegans') takes the vosotros verb form.

52.tr: You're so silly! (laughs) Well, is there anything else in the recipe that caught your attention, that surprised you?
v: llamar la atención = to catch someone's attention.
o: you (the Englishman): it caught YOUR attention
g: hay = there is; algo más = something else.
x: to catch someone's attention; to stand out (te llamó la atención = it caught your eye)

53.tr: Of course! I was also amazed when your mother told me there were three kinds of meat in the paella: chicken, rabbit and duck.
g: After a past reporting verb the present hay often becomes imperfect había.

54.tr: Rabbit is another animal I've never eaten, never tried.
o: relative = otro animal (that I have never eaten)

55.tr: Spanish people like it a lot.
v: Singular: the thing liked is el conejo.
o: los españoles — doubled: A los españoles les gusta
g: a + person + les + gusta: the person appears twice; les is required.

56.tr: Is it common to eat it in the United Kingdom?
v: es + adjective + infinitive: it is common to…
g: Impersonal: es frecuente / es normal / es fácil + infinitive.

57.tr: I think you can find it in some specialist shop, but it's definitely not common to eat it.
g: tú is often used for 'people in general', like English 'you can find it…'.

58.tr: You're not going to find it in Tesco Express, for example.
g: lo vas a encontrar = vas a encontrarlo. Both positions are correct.

59.tr: OK, right… And so, that day when you met my family, you didn't only learn the original paella recipe, you also learnt an unwritten rule about Spanish culture, didn't you?
v: conocer (preterite) = met for the first time.
o: una regla o una norma no escrita
g: Not only … but also. Use sino que before a conjugated verb.
ese día en el que = that day when/on which.
¿verdad? at the end = right? / didn't you?

x: that's right, that's how it is

63.tr: Well, basically I ate a lot, too much.

64.tr: Your mother served me a very big plate of paella; I ate it and finished it like a good, polite Englishman.
v: Stem change e → i in the 3rd person preterite (sirvió).
g: Sequence of events in the preterite
A chain of completed actions in a story → preterite.
educado = polite, well-mannered; 'educated' is culto / con estudios.

o: el plato de paella — doubled by todo: lo comí todo
g: With todo as object Spanish adds lo: lo comí todo = I ate it all.

66.tr: She, naturally, asked me if I had liked it, and I said yes.
v: si me había gustado = whether I had liked it.
o: me: whether it had pleased ME (gustar)
g: '¿Te ha gustado?' becomes 'si me había gustado' when reported in the past.
To say yes / no: dije que sí.

67.tr: She asked me if I wanted more paella and I didn't know what to say…
v: no sabía qué decir = I didn't know what to say.
g: no sé qué decir = I don't know what to say (correctly written qué, with accent).

68.tr: But if you were full you should have said no, that you didn't want much more, that you'd eaten enough and that you were full.
v: tenías que haber dicho = you should have said.
g: A criticism about the past: you should have done (but didn't).
estar lleno = to be full (after eating).

69.tr: When we want to ask someone for something and be polite, we can use the formula: ¿Podrías + a verb?
v: pedir algo a alguien = to ask someone for something.
Conditional for polite requests: could you…?
g: pedir = ask FOR something; preguntar = ask a question.

71.tr: Could you give me (lit. put me / serve me) a little more food, not much please?
g: poquito softens the request: just a little bit.

72.tr: Could you pass me the bread, please?

73.tr: Could you tell me where that street is, please?
g: dónde keeps its accent inside the sentence.

o: neuter lo = what you just said (that I should say no)
g: lo sé = I know (it). lo refers to an idea, not a noun.

75.tr: Well, I know now, but at that moment I didn't want to seem rude.
v: Imperfect for a wish/attitude at that past moment.
o: neuter lo: the rule just explained
g: Describes his state of mind at that moment.

76.tr: It was the first time I saw your mother.
v: In 'la primera vez que…' Spanish often uses the imperfect (or preterite).

77.tr: I thought saying no to her offer was rude, and I wanted your mother to like me.
v: Imperfect for a belief in the past.
Infinitive as subject: decir no era maleducado.
quería gustarle a tu madre = I wanted your mother to like me (lit. to please her).
o: tu madre — doubled: gustarle a tu madre
g: Here the speaker is the subject: I want to please her = I want her to like me.

78.tr: So I said yes and she served me another whole plate.

80.tr: And at that point my stomach was starting to hurt.
v: Imperfect for a process in progress: it was starting to…
g: me duele el estómago = my stomach hurts. Use the article (el estómago), not a possessive.

81.tr: And she asked me again if I wanted more.

82.tr: Oh my God! And what did you say?

83.tr: Well, I told her yes, but obviously I said I only wanted a little more, that I only had room for a tiny bit more.

84.tr: And again she served me another plate.

85.tr: I was very, very, very full, so I had to say no.
v: tuve que = I had to (and did): a completed obligation.
g: tuve que decir = I had to say (and I did); tenía que = I was supposed to (maybe not done).

86.tr: I was really full, I was going to explode! (laughs)
g: Something about to happen in the past.

87.tr: Well, now you know, but Spain has a fairly direct culture.
o: neuter lo: the rule about saying no
g: ya = now (after a change): now you know (it).

88.tr: You British speak in a more indirect way, but Spaniards don't.
g: de una forma … = in a … way. forma is feminine, so indirecta agrees.

89.tr: It's fine if you say you don't want to eat more, because otherwise they'll keep offering you food, as you already know.
v: te attached to the gerund (accent added).
como ya sabes = as you already know.
g: Pronouns attach to gerunds and get a written accent: ofreciéndote.

90.tr: I'm very Spanish in that respect.

91.tr: If I cook something for guests I'm afraid they'll be hungry, so I keep offering them more and more food.
v: Subjunctive after tener miedo de que (fear).

94.tr: By the way, speaking of this, I've remembered what you have to do with food in China.
v: hablando de esto = speaking of this.
me he acordado de = I've remembered.
g: Pronominal verb + de: me acuerdo de… = I remember…
Impersonal obligation: what one has to do.
lo que hay que hacer = what you have to do.

95.tr: I lived in China for a few months, and apparently it's good manners to leave a little food on your plate.
v: A closed period of time (unos meses).
g: A finished period (a few months) → preterite, even if it lasted a while.

96.tr: It's a sign, on one hand, that you're full and can't eat any more — they've given you enough food — and, on the other, that you liked the food, because you've eaten almost all of it.
v: te ha gustado = you liked it.
g: Recent result: you have eaten almost all of it.
With todo/toda as object add the pronoun: la has comido toda.

v: Imperfect for knowledge/state in the past (up to now).
o: neuter lo: what was just explained
g: Standard way to say 'I didn't know (that)'.

99.tr: Maybe in another episode you can tell us about your experiences in China learning Chinese.

v: Conditional = would: me encantaría = I'd love to.
g: Polite, enthusiastic acceptance: I'd love to.
Adjectives like bueno often go before the noun; agrees: una buena idea.

102.tr: Now we have to say goodbye, say adiós.
g: despedirse = to say goodbye; the pronoun matches the subject: tenemos que despedirnos.

103.tr: Yes, we hope you've enjoyed this first episode of the podcast "Spanish for False Beginners".
v: te haya gustado = you have enjoyed it.
g: Hope about something already completed: we hope you've liked it.
primero → primer before a masculine singular noun.

104.tr: We'll hear each other in the next episode.
v: Present with future meaning; reciprocal nos.
g: nos escuchamos = we hear each other (a podcast version of nos vemos).

105.tr: Remember you can read the transcripts and use the vocabulary flashcards for the episodes at www.spanishlanguagecoach.com.
v: Affirmative command (same form as él present).
g: The tú command = 3rd person singular present: recuerda, escucha, lee.

106.tr: If you've enjoyed the episode, you can leave a comment or some stars on your podcast platform.
v: te ha gustado = you have liked.
dejar un comentario = leave a comment.
o: you: if it has pleased YOU
g: Real condition about something just experienced.

107.tr: Thank you very much! A big hug!
x: lit. a hug: a warm, informal sign-off (like 'take care')

108.tr: A hug! Until the next episode!
x: hasta + time/event = see you …: hasta luego, hasta mañana
